items.title: Bob Cranshaw interviewed by Michael Woods, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995
items.q: And so Clark Terry and a lot of these guys that a lot of people don’t know were in these bands.

ctx.x: Now I want to come back in and say you said that there was a lot of things going on, a lot of trouble that a young man could get into. But the music and the masters of the music kept you away from it. Elaborate on that.

Well Milt Hinton was one of the masters. One of the things that was funny, when I came to New York I came, I had a decent bass, but I had a bass case that was so raggedy. I mean it was in bad shape. And I used to go to clubs until Milton looked at this bass case and he said, “Son, you can’t be going around with a case like this.” So he donated a, he gave me a bass bag. ‘Cause he was embarrassed. But it showed me, I mean he was just so, his demeanor at that time. When I came to New York, there was a lot of jobs.…

situation happening. But the Milt Hintons and people like that they were just, they were wonderful. I mean Milt Hinton, I still, he’s just marvelous. He’s just a marvelous person. And I wanted to be Milt Hinton. I wanted to be this. The next Milt Hinton was my dream. I just wanted to be like he was. And Joe and Milt and all of them were very close. So hearing their experiences, trying to re-live some of the experiences that I had heard them talk about, and so forth, was just wonderful. And I think I caught maybe…
